summary: Ephemeral runner delegate credential regeneration blocks nightly release jobs
summary_long: During a scheduled Vault rewrap/credential epoch roll, a subset of ephemeral CI runners failed to receive regenerated delegate credentials and were unable to start jobs for the nightly release pipeline. This caused a ~25% failure rate in the nightly release matrix for packages requiring artifact signing and slowed the release by ~3 hours.
impact: Nightly release jobs that require impersonation to the signing bastion or access to internal artifact buckets failed to start or timed out. Production artifacts were delayed; release owner escalated to SRE and Release Engineering.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger ephemeral runner bootstrap after a Vault rewrap event (simulated with vault rewrap token).
2) Provision runner pods with delegate-role annotation pointing at the ephemeral service-account.
3) Observe kubelet logs for injector container and check runner heartbeat.
4) Attempt to queue a nightly_release job that needs signing-bastion access.
Expected: runner obtains regenerated delegate credential and job starts.
Observed: runner reports credential fetch error and remains Pending
logs_and_errors:
[2026-03-10T01:12:03Z] injector: vault-sidecar: failed to unwrap token: ciphertext mismatch
[2026-03-10T01:12:04Z] runner-bootstrap: credential-watcher: no new delegate token found for SA ephemeral-runner-ztg-02; last_epoch=2026-03-09T23:00:00Z
[2026-03-10T01:12:10Z] ci-controller: job queue: runner none available for label = signing+bastion -> queued
[2026-03-10T01:15:21Z] runner: kubelet: pod crashloopbackoff; exit 128: failed to start: auth: delegate token missing
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: Vault rewrap produced mixed epochs and the sidecar unwrap policy didn't accept the new ciphertext. We correlated runner bootstrap failures with Vault operator window 2026-03-10T00:55Z-01:10Z. Not all pods failed; failures concentrated on nodes that had pod eviction and were reprovisioned during the rewrap.
Checked K8s events: majority of failing pods were scheduled onto node-pool-autoscaler nodes which had transient network flaps. Also observed ephemeral service-account tokens in K8s remained bound to old token hash until kube-controller-manager re-synced.
Auth team reproduced unwrap error locally using rewrap ciphertext from operator logs; unwrap succeeds when using Vault token with explicit "rewrap" capability. Suspect token wrapping config didn't include new delegate role in rotation policy during the epoch change.
root_cause: A timing window during the Vault rewrap combined with node reprovisioning caused injector sidecars to request wrapped tokens against an intermediate key. The policy applied to the rewrap job did not include the delegate-service-account role for ephemeral runners created mid-epoch, so the unwrap operation returned a ciphertext-mismatch. Additionally, kube-controller-manager's token projection cache delayed the SA token swap on reprovisioned nodes, amplifying failures.
workaround:
1) Manually trigger vault unwrap for affected pods using operator rewrap token (ops-only).
2) Restart affected runner pods after forcing SA token refresh: kubectl delete pod <runner-pod> --namespace=ci; pods rebootstrap and obtain new token.
3) For queued release jobs, temporarily allow fallback routing to standby signing runners with long-lived credentials (route flagged by release team).
permanent_fix_plan:
Short term: patch Vault rewrap job to include ephemeral-runner delegate role in rotation policy and ensure unwrap compatibility across epochs. Implement a post-rewrap webhook that signals the runner-provisioner to refresh projected tokens.
Medium term: make injector sidecar unwrap idempotent across overlapping epochs (try unwrap with both old and new wrapping keys). Add a controller to watch SA token projection changes and proactively restart pods with stale projections. Add chaos tests that reprovision nodes during credential-roll windows.
Owners: auth-team (policy patch), infra-sre (kube token refresh controller), runner-team (injector idempotency). Target ETA: 2 weeks for policy + webhook, 6 weeks for controller and injector change.
resolution: In progress: policy updated in vault-operator PR 188 and manual restarts performed for the 18 affected pods. Release team rerouted signing jobs to standby signing runners. Root causes tracked to infra and auth; full fix scheduled as described.
